summary.overview: The Project Amazon PH Academy v2 harness has a working Next.js + Prisma signup pipeline with CI, architecture tests, and bounded coverage gates, but the most material core path returns an untyped error on the documented smoketest, the dev scripts bypass the only sanctioned PrismaClient site, and the Project Skill contradicts the AGENTS.md canon. Recovery, in-place core boundary, and per-area AGENTS.md ownership stay absent.

assignmentSummaries.title: Signup happy path: typed `verification_required` replaces canonical `unexpected` at the action boundary
assignmentSummaries.body: Signup succeeded but the auto-login could not mint a session for the new UNVERIFIED account. The canonical `unexpected` return at the action boundary was replaced with the typed `verification_required` member, with the wrapper routing to the verify-email sent page. Vitest signup tests 12 of 12 pass including the new regression case; full suite 3888 of 3888 with no regressions; tsc and eslint clean; asset-integrity reviewed with 0 findings; STORY-005 status updated.

The current failure path leaves the user-facing error untyped and bypasses the typed error contract that `signup.action.test.ts` mocks around. The agent-recorded smoketest report is in the diff as an untracked file, so the regression is invisible to PR review.

findings.title: Untracked dev scripts construct PrismaClient outside the sanctioned site
findings.reason: Four untracked JavaScript files in `scripts/` instantiate `new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg(pool) })` directly. AGENTS.md and the in-code rule forbid `new PrismaClient()` outside `src/infra/database/prisma.ts`, and the boundary ESLint rule only walks `src/`, so the scripts bypass the port, use case, and audit-log hooks. Because the files are untracked, they will not be reviewed in any PR and any schema drift between them and the production migration set is invisible to the build.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Gate owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Move the untracked `scripts/*.cjs` files through the project composition root, or add a scripts-level boundary check that fails the local lint when a script calls `new PrismaClient()` directly. Keep the rule bounded to the canonical owner.

## Validation

- Run `pnpm lint` and confirm the new boundary rule flags the offending scripts.
- Run the focused e2e job and confirm the rewritten scripts still seed the same fixtures.

findings.title: Production wiring surfaces are excluded from the Vitest coverage gate
findings.reason: `vitest.config.ts` excludes `src/composition/container.ts`, all `src/infra/repositories/Prisma*.ts`, `src/infra/payment/Prisma*.ts`, and `src/infra/database/prisma.ts` from the line coverage gate. A regression in `PrismaUserRepository.create` (which maps Prisma error code `P2002` to `kind: email_taken` by string compare) is not caught by a dedicated unit test; the only coverage is the contract pin in `signup.action.test.ts`'s `email_taken` case, which goes through the in-memory adapter.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Test owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add one focused unit test for `PrismaUserRepository.create` that maps Prisma error code `P2002` to `kind: email_taken`. Keep the test in `src/infra/repositories/__tests__/` and run only against the Prisma adapter, not the in-memory one.

## Validation

- Run `pnpm test:unit` and confirm the new test passes.
- Confirm the focused test fails when the Prisma error code mapping is removed.

findings.title: Project Skill `amph-v2-greenfield` contradicts AGENTS.md
findings.reason: `.agents/skills/amph-v2-greenfield/SKILL.md` is missing a YAML frontmatter description (lint warning `skill-missing-description`) and its body claims the testing framework is `unknown` and that the only observed prefix is `docs`, both directly contradicted by the same-project `AGENTS.md` (Vitest + Playwright; conventional commits `feat`/`fix`/`refactor`/`docs`/`test`/`chore`). The Skill is configured but its content routes future agents to incorrect context.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Skill owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add a YAML frontmatter description to `.agents/skills/amph-v2-greenfield/SKILL.md` and update the body so it references the canonical Vitest + Playwright stack and the conventional commit prefixes from `AGENTS.md`. Keep the diff scoped to this Skill file.

## Validation

- Run `pnpm exec qoder agent-lint --json` and confirm the `skill-missing-description` warning is gone.
- Open the updated Skill and confirm the testing framework and prefix claims match `AGENTS.md`.

findings.title: Core boundary is inferred rather than curated
findings.reason: `coreCodeRules.status: missing` with `boundaryKind: inferred-core-boundary` means the core boundary the scanner uses to flag churn is whatever the inference logic produces, not what the project owner has declared. Agent readers will treat the inferred boundary as if it were authored, so the high-churn hotspots (`src/composition/container.ts` 77 commits / 1840 churn, `src/app/actions/signup.action.ts` 12 commits / 699 churn, `src/infra/repositories/PrismaUserRepository.ts` 12 commits / 341 churn) are not flagged against an authoritative core list.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Config owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add a curated `coreCodeRules` configuration file (e.g. `.qoder/code-rules.json`) that lists the files the project owner considers core, and wire the scanner to read it before inferring. Keep the boundary narrow and reflect the documented core boundary (composition root, signup action, use cases, Prisma adapters).

## Validation

- Run the project-aware scanner and confirm the curated boundary is read.
- Confirm the current high-churn hotspots are flagged as configured core, not inferred.
